subject: Dedicated capacity: burst policy, slab sizing and mutual action plan
messages:
From: Lena Zhao <lena.z@hyperthrive.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity planning: burst profile & autoscale ask

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week — the team was impressed by the latency guarantees on Dedicated. We're now working through capacity planning for our Q1 load and need to lock the burst/autoscale policy details before the contract signature. A few specifics: 

- Expected steady-state: 120 concurrent generation pods (p99 latency target 250ms)
- Anticipated weekly peak events: 20-30 minute spikes 2x/week that multiply token throughput by ~4x
- Two scheduled seasonal surges (marketing pushes) ~3 hours each calendar month

Key asks:
1) Can Redwood guarantee an autoscale ramp to 4x steady within 90 seconds for ephemeral bursts?
2) How are burst credits consumed & replenished for Dedicated customers? Any hard caps?
3) Proposal for a safety slab (ephemeral GPUs) to absorb peaks without impacting core slab SLAs

I've attached our usage profile spreadsheet (hyperthrive_burst_profile_v1.xlsx) to help. Would like to sync with your capacity/product folks and get a write-up we can attach to procurement.

Thanks,
Lena
Director, Platform Ops
HyperThrive AI

(Attachment: hyperthrive_burst_profile_v1.xlsx)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Zhao <lena.z@hyperthrive.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning: burst profile & autoscale ask

Lena — thanks for the clear profile and for putting the numbers together. I reviewed the sheet quickly and looped in Karthik and Ben to propose a technical + commercial approach. Quick responses inline: 

1) Autoscale ramp: realistic ramp depends on your reservation size and whether you can accept short pre-warm windows. With our dedicated slab + ephemeral shoulder pool model we can achieve a 90s effective ramp for cold requests if we pre-warm a small standby KV cache set; otherwise warm-only requests can hit 90s for instance provisioning but token p99 may vary.

2) Burst credits: we offer two constructs — a replenishing credit bank (daily top-up) and a bounded monthly overage bucket. For Dedicated customers we can set a configurable monthly burst cap and an emergency override with a negotiated price. We'll propose concrete numbers after Karthik sizes the slab and shoulder pool.

3) Safety slab proposal: suggest a two-tier slab — primary reserved GPUs sized for 120 concurrent generators + 25% buffer, plus an ephemeral shoulder pool sized at 3x steady concurrency but subject to preemptible eviction and a soft SLO.

Can we book a technical call Monday for an hour? Karthik — can you draft a sizing table + timeline for pre-warm vs pure spin-up? Ben — will loop you for pricing & proposed credit banding.

Thanks,
Mateo
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

(Attached: rdw_prod_sizing.pdf - initial sizing sketch)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Lena Zhao <lena.z@hyperthrive.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning: burst profile & autoscale ask

Lena / team — I ran the spreadsheet through our sizing model and sketched three options (summary below). See attached mutual_action_plan_hyperthrive.docx for the recommended runway and operational steps.

Option A (Conservative):
- Primary slab: 150 reserved GPUs (covers 120 concurrent generators at 25% headroom)
- Shoulder pool: 450 ephemeral GPUs (3x steady concurrency)
- Autoscale behavior: instant routing to shoulder pool for identified spike signatures; full spin-up fallback within 120s
- Burst credit usage: shoulder pool consumes monthly burst bucket; credit rate = 0.7x standard per-GPU unit (preemptible pricing)

Option B (Balanced) - Recommended:
- Primary slab: 140 reserved GPUs (+16% buffer)
- Shoulder pool: 300 ephemeral GPUs (2.5x steady)
- Autoscale: pre-warm + continuous batching enables effective 90s ramp for common paths; fallback spin-up <180s
- Credits: combination of daily micro-topups (replenish at midnight) + monthly overage bucket with auto-notify at 70% usage

Option C (Aggressive cost-optimized):
- Primary slab: 120 reserved GPUs (match steady)
- Shoulder pool: 400 ephemeral GPUs, higher eviction risk
- Autoscale: relies heavily on shoulder pool; longer cold-starts for unusual model variants

Operational notes:
- We recommend a pre-warm plan for the top 10% of your model endpoints (based on your sheet) which reduces p99 latency variance during bursts.
- We'll instrument token-level tracing to charge only for active generation tokens when shoulder pool is used.
- We propose a monthly burst cap by default (configurable) with a one-time emergency override route (manual approval) for sudden market events.

I'll be on the call Monday 10:00 PST to walk through the sizing table if that works.

Cheers,
Karthik
Director, Dedicated Platforms
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: mutual_action_plan_hyperthrive.docx)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lena Zhao <lena.z@hyperthrive.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 11:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning: burst profile & autoscale ask

Lena — adding the commercial lens. Based on Karthik's Option B (balanced) here's the proposed deal language for the SOW: 

- Reserved capacity: monthly fee covering primary slab (140 GPUs) with a committed usage SLA (monthly uptime 99.5%).
- Shoulder pool & burst credits: monthly baseline credit allocation sized to expected spikes (we recommend a starting 20% monthly buffer). Overage billing at the negotiated per-GPU-minute rate; emergency override capped at 2x monthly burst bucket and requires exec sign-off.
- Pre-warm credits: small recurring charge for maintaining pre-warm KV cache on 10% of endpoints; reduces p99 during spikes (not counted against burst bucket).

We can offer a first-year promotional credit equal to one month of shoulder pool usage if HyperThrive signs by Jan 15 and commits to a 12-month reserved term. I'll put this into the quote and update the HubSpot deal.

Would like to confirm the acceptance criteria you need for procurement to sign — e.g., headroom math, explicit preemption behavior, and emergency override SLA.

Best,
Ben
Head of Customer Deals
Redwood Inference

(Attachment referenced: commercial_quote_vRDW-3971.pdf - will send after internal approval)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Zhao <lena.z@hyperthrive.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 11:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity planning: burst profile & autoscale ask

Lena — great sync today, and thanks everyone for rapid follow-up. Recap / mutual action plan agreed on the call: 

- Go with Option B (Balanced) as baseline: primary slab 140 GPUs + shoulder pool 300 GPUs.
- Autoscale SLO: target 90s effective ramp for common endpoints with pre-warm for top 10%; spin-up fallback <180s.
- Burst credits: daily micro-topups + monthly overage bucket; will start with a 20% monthly buffer and telemetry to notify at 70% consumption.
- Commercial: Ben to include 1 month promotional shoulder credit in the quote for signatures by 2027-01-15.
- Next steps: Redwood to provide a signed SOW draft (commercial quote + appendix with operational playbook) and HyperThrive to provide procurement contact and any required SOC artifacts.

I'll drop the SOW + appendix in the shared Drive link and ping procurement contact (cc list below) once ready. Thanks all — ping here if anything is off.

Mateo
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
